messages:
carla: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a CANARY DB migration for orders_service at 10:15 PT. It's a safe additive change (new column `legacy_order` boolean) plus a small backfill. Need final rollback criteria, pin for the service route, and short release-note blurb. Will run canary for 30m on low-traffic hosts.
ben: ACK. Thanks for the heads-up. For rollback thresholds: do we want error-rate-based or latency-based aborts?
alice: I'd combine both. Proposal: abort the canary if any of: 1) query error rate > 0.8% sustained for 2 minutes, 2) p99 latency > baseline + 250ms for 3 consecutive mins, 3) any exclusive lock > 500ms, 4) replica lag > 2s for more than 1 minute, or 5) backfill row failure rate > 0.1%.
carla: That looks reasonable. Add one more: if we see > 3 deadlocks in 5m or a single rolling restart of a replica node.
ben: +1. Also recommend a soft-fallback: if metric breach is minor (error spike 0.5-0.8%) we auto-scale canary hosts down to 1 host and keep watching for 10m before full abort.
carla: Good idea — we'll set a two-step: soft throttled fallback then hard abort. I'll put those in the release notes and ticket.
ops: I've pinned the canary route to service version `orders@3.8.2-canary` and created feature flag `orders.migrate_legacy_order` set to OFF. We'll flip to ON only after the canary DB migration succeeds.
carla: deploybot, please start the migration canary and annotate CI with the rollback criteria.
deploybot: deploybot: scheduled canary (id: canary-178888) started on hosts [ord-canary-1, ord-canary-2]. Migration job queued: orders.add_legacy_order_v2. Monitoring for 30m.
sre-bot: Observability checklist posted to channel dashboard: https://infra.internal/dashboard/ordermig — watch p95/p99, error-rate, DB lock-timeouts, replica_lag, and backfill_fail_rate. Alerting thresholds set to the criteria Alice listed.
ben: Quick rollback runbook (condensed):
```
# soft-fallback
1) set feature flag orders.migrate_legacy_order = OFF
2) scale canary instances to 1 via console (route pin remains)
# hard-rollback (if abort condition persists)
1) pause traffic to canary route: `routes pinch orders-canary`
2) run rollback SQL: `psql -d orders -c "ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS legacy_order;"`
3) revert service pin to `orders@3.8.1` and redeploy if needed
4) run backfill cleanup: `python tools/backfill_cleanup.py --job orders.add_legacy_order_v2 --revert`
```
carla: I'll add that to the runbook and update ticket #ORD-1234 with the pinned version and rollback steps. Release-note blurb draft: "Add `legacy_order` column to orders to support new fulfillment flow; canary migration 30m; rollback criteria and runbook in ticket."
alice: Ack from infra side. I vetted the SQL, and the backfill uses batched updates of 500 rows to avoid long-held locks. We should monitor the batch duration and stop if avg batch > 2s.
ops: Feature flag ready to toggle. I'll stand by for flip and will annotate the ticket with timestamps.
deploybot: canary-178888 reports: health=OK, backfill batch rate ~ 450 rows/second, avg batch time 1.6s, errors=0.1% (within soft thresholds).
carla: thanks — @alice @ben please give thumbs-up when you're comfortable to proceed past initial 10m observation.
alice: thumbs-up :+1: observed metrics look stable at 12m.
ben: thumbs-up :+1: agree.
carla: proceeding to full canary run. Will post a short postmortem if anything weird happens and update release notes + ORD-1234.
deploybot: canary-178888 still healthy at 25m. No abort triggers observed.
carla: closing the thread for now — will reopen if rollback executed. Thanks everyone.
